Pt c/o difficulty managing at home post-laminectomy, 47d s/p discharge. Wife working full-time unable to provide assistance w/ ADLs and mobility support during day. Pt denies other family members or friends available for help. Lives w/ spouse only. States managing pain adequately on current regimen but cannot perform necessary activities independently. Discussed options including home health referral, pt to follow up w/ surgeon regarding discharge plan modifications.

pt called today 19d s/p lumbar laminectomy. c/o incision opening up at site, says sutures appear to be coming apart. denies fever, purulent drainage, or increased pain beyond baseline. instructed pt to monitor for signs of infection and call back if worsening. VM left for surgery clinic regarding need for evaluation.

Pt called today d/p 9 days. Reports walker ordered at discharge has not arrived yet. Pt also states bedroom commode that was delivered is broken - seat will not lock in place. Instructed pt to contact DME vendor directly re: walker ETA and commode malfunction. Pt c/o difficulty ambulating safely pending equipment resolution.

Pt called reporting loose stools x 2-3 wks, increasing in frequency over past few days. Denies fever or blood. Takes abx s/p knee replacement 92d ago, unsure of d/c date on abx course. Advised to contact PCP re: stool changes given recent abx use, discussed need for hydration. VM left for PCP ROV.
No answer on first attempt 10:15am, VM left requesting pt/CG call back today re post-op status.

CG called back 2:30pm reports pt c/o incision site opening up, says stitches appear to be coming apart s/p hernia repair 5d ago. Pt noting some drainage, denies fever or severe pain. Instructed CG to notify surgeon today, no VM ROV, advised to seek urgent eval if increased drainage/signs of infection. Will follow up tomorrow AM.
POD#3 f/u call, pt states unclear on what she can/cannot do w/ lifting, driving, activities--denies receipt of d/c instructions, will resend info to pt.
POD#6 call. Pt c/o heart racing w/ skipped beats intermittently. Denies CP, SOB, or lightheadedness. Instructed to call PCP tomorrow, VM left for cardiology.

Pt called for post-d/c f/u on POD 11 s/p colectomy. Reports ongoing queasiness & vomiting x 3-4 days, worsening after meals. Denies fever, abd pain, or diarrhea. Tolerating sips of water & broth. Advised to try small frequent meals, ginger, & call back if worsens or unable to keep down fluids. VM left w/ surgical team for eval if symptoms persist past wknd.
Pt c/o unclear on timing of cardiac meds post-CABG, states has bottles but not taking as directed. Instructed on importance, pt to start today and contact if questions.
Pt caregiver reached on second attempt. VM left at 11:20a requesting call back today.

Caregiver reports that home health nurse has not yet initiated visits despite discharge orders placed 13d ago. Pt waiting at home for contact from VNA agency but has not heard from them. Caregiver unaware of what to do next and concerned visits are not scheduled. Advised caregiver to contact VNA agency directly with discharge summary info and provided contact number. Explained pt should expect call from agency w/in 24-48hrs to schedule initial eval.

Pt called c/o loose stools x several days, freq 3-4x/day, started after d/c antibiotics s/p hernia repair. Denies abd pain, fever, blood in stool. Advised fluids, probiotics, call back if worsens or fever develops.

POD#2 called by daughter. Pt c/o sharp pain in lower abdomen x 2 days, denies recent trauma or fall. Pain worse w/ movement, currently 6/10, tried acetaminophen PRN w/ minimal relief. No associated nausea, diarrhea, or fever. Tolerating regular diet. Daughter c/c appears well otherwise but concerned re: pain duration. Advised to contact primary care today or ED if pain worsens, inability to void, or fever develops. No intervention needed at this time per ROV protocol.
Called pt 9d s/p DC, c/o hasn't had any visits from home health nurse yet despite discharge orders. Pt states no one has contacted him to schedule.

Pt called today 11d s/p d/c, doing ok overall. Mentioned his daughter was visiting from out of state so been nice to have family around. Asked how knee surgery recovery going, pt says pain managed ok with OTC ibuprofen mostly. Transitioned to talking about his new meds and filled most of them but says the lisinopril script is just too expensive right now, insurance won't cover much of it and the copay is like 200 bucks a month for a 90 day supply so hasn't filled it yet. Said his wife was hassling him about it but money's tight with property taxes due soon. Denies any chest pain, SOB, or swelling in legs. Encouraged him to contact his PCP about generic options or pt assistance programs, gave him number to call. Will follow up end of next week, asked him to really try to get something worked out on that BP med before then. Weather's been nice there he said. Will VM if no one home.

Pt's caregiver called for 14d post-d/c f/u. Reports pt having difficulty obtaining prescribed metoprolol d/t financial constraints. Pt able to pick up rx but stretching doses to make last longer. Denies s/x of angina or HTN urgency at this time. Caregiver aware may need assistance w/ medication costs. RVU PCP for possible generic alt or patient assistance program.

Pt called with c/o about chest tube. States dressing is weeping serous fluid, soaked through two times since d/c 2 days ago. Denies fever, cp, SOB. Instructed pt to keep area clean and dry, change dressing PRN, monitor for increasing output or signs of infection. Will f/u ROV in 2 days or sooner if worsening. Pt verbalized understanding.
VM left at 10:15a asking pt to call back when available, advised he had questions re: home care setup s/p discharge.

Pt called back around 2p, said he was out running errands with his daughter, just got home. Nice day out so they drove around a bit, she brought him some groceries. Went through discharge plan again, pt says he's been doing OK pain-wise, took his new meds without issue, denies any fever or shortness of breath. Then I asked about the visiting nurse and he said nobody has called him yet, doesn't know when they're coming. Said he expected someone would show up yesterday or today but nothing. Checked his discharge paperwork and the order went through from hospital, so should have been scheduled. Pt denies getting any phone call from the agency, no VM left that he heard of. Also mentioned his back is still bothering him from before all this, says the heating pad helps. Advised pt I would follow up with agency directly and call him back with a time window, said to expect initial visit within 24 hrs. Pt agreed, said his daughter will be here to let them in if he's not around. Pt in good spirits, no other c/o at this time.

Pt called reporting episodes of racing and skipped heartbeats x 3 days, onset 10 days post-d/c, no associated CP or SOB, denies palpitations prior to discharge, states timing irregular and unpredictable. Advised ROV with PCP, VM left for provider callback.
VM left 10/14 @ 1430 requesting pt call back regarding post-d/c f/u. Caregiver (daughter) returned call @ 1645.

Caregiver verbalized that pt unsure how to perform wound dressing changes at home. Reviewed dressing change technique and care instructions by phone. Instructed caregiver to contact clinic if pt has further questions or dressing site shows signs of infection. Will monitor via follow-up contact.

Pt called today ~10wks s/p CABG. C/o cramping and soreness in lower abd x 2-3 wks, denies N/V, denies diarrhea or constipation, taking PRN tylenol w/ minimal relief. States pain not near incision sites, waxes and wanes throughout day. Denies fever, trauma, or recent falls. Instructed to contact PCP for further eval, given timeframe and persistence. Pt verbalized understanding and will call office tomorrow.

Pt called today, 5d s/p D/C. C/o unable to obtain home meds at pharmacy - states insurer is holding Rx pending prior auth from MD office. Pt denies symptoms or concerns otherwise. Advised pt to contact prescriber office directly to expedite auth process. VM left w/ covering MD to follow up on pending auth.

Called pt at home today, 7 days post d/c. Pt states doing okay overall, weather been nice where she lives, mentioned her grandson visited last week. She c/o some ongoing discomfort at surgical site but says manageable w/ current pain regimen. Main issue: pt tried reaching surgeon's office multiple times this past week regarding question about her incision, kept getting VM, no one called her back. Also tried contacting her PCP for refill authorization and got same story - VM, never ROV. Separately mentioned her knee's been acting up but that's chronic. Pt denies fever, denies n/v, denies increased drainage or redness at site. She's frustrated bc she wasn't sure if what she's seeing is normal or if she should be worried. Explained VM protocol and recommended she call surgeon first thing Monday morning, offered to place call for her if needed. Pt felt reassured, said she'll try again in am. Will follow up end of week if she doesn't report back.
Called pt residence at 2:15p, caregiver answered. Pt resting, caregiver stated they would be available for call back around 4p today.

Caregiver c/o pt noticing dark stool x 2-3 days, also reports pt vomited once yesterday and there was dark material in the vomit. Caregiver denies pt c/o abdominal pain currently. Pt on coumadin s/p CABG. Advised caregiver to contact PCP today and d/c to ED if increased bleeding, dark stools continue, or any further vomiting. Caregiver verbalized understanding. ROV advised.

Called pt today 2 weeks post-d/c. Pt doing ok physically, wound healing well, no c/o of pain today. Got to talking about how things are at home and pt mentioned the apartment is pretty rough right now - roof's been leaking since the rain last week, water coming through in the bedroom. Pt says landlord keeps saying he'll get someone out but nothing yet. Also mentioned the steps out front are broken and pretty dangerous, pt has been careful going up and down but worried about falling. We talked for a bit about the weather, pt says it's been rainy here too which isn't helping with the roof situation. Pt's daughter called yesterday wanting to know how the recovery is going. Pt concerned that with all the moisture from the leak the place isn't great for healing up. Heat hasn't been reliable either past few days. Pt denies any new symptoms but clearly worried about the living situation and how long this will all get sorted out. VM to follow up with SW re: resources.
VM left on first attempt at 1420h, pt's daughter called back at 1530h

Daughter reports pt c/o heart feels like it's racing and skipping beats, started yesterday PM. Denies cp, sob, or dizziness. Advised to contact PCP today, instructed daughter on warning signs and when to call 911

Pt called reporting unusual bruising on bilateral arms and legs started 3 days ago, denies trauma. Also c/o increased nosebleeds x2 in past week. On apixaban post-discharge s/p DVT event. Pt unsure if bruising/bleeding is normal on this med. Advised to contact anticoag clinic today to discuss INR stability and whether dose adjustment needed. VM left for PCP to call back regarding bleeding concerns, ROV anticoag clinic tomorrow.

Pt called c/o not yet received post-op pain med refill. States pharmacist advised insurer req prior auth before releasing script. Pt reports incision healing well, no drainage or increased pain. Instructed pt to contact surgeon office to facilitate auth process w/ insurance. ROV pending resolution.
Called pt at 2:15pm, no answer. VM left asking pt to call back at earliest convenience regarding post-d/c follow-up.

Pt called back around 4pm. States doing okay overall, incision healing well, no drainage or signs of infection. Weather has been nice so got out in the yard a bit yesterday which felt good. Daughter visiting from out of state next month which he's excited about. When asked about appt with Dr. Martinez scheduled for next Thursday at 2pm, pt states he has conflict - his wife has her chemo treatment that same afternoon and he's her driver, can't reschedule her appt. Pt was adamant about this, said his priority is getting wife to her treatment on time. Denies any new c/o s/p discharge, no fever, tolerating diet well, meds refilled and taking as prescribed. Discussed need to get rescheduled soon and pt agrees, said he'll call office himself tomorrow morning to work out new time. Advised to call back if any concerns arise before next contact. Call ended on good terms.

Pt called for post-op f/u s/p appendectomy, 45 days post-discharge. C/o wound care questions. Pt denies understanding how to change the dressing at home or what to look for w/ incision care. Instructed on dressing changes, signs of infection, and when to contact surgeon. Pt verbalized understanding. VM left w/ surgeon's office for any questions PRN.

Pt called c/o persistent dizziness and lightheadedness x 2 wks, denies falls. States symptoms started after restart of BP med post-d/c. Denies chest pain, SOB, or syncope. Pt tolerating POs well, ambulating independently at home. Advised to contact MD re: possible med adjustment and d/c'd to ROV.

Pt called today 13d s/p d/c. Doing ok overall, recovering well at home. Weather has been nice which is good bc pt says they're trying to get out more. Mentioned their daughter is visiting next month which they're excited about. When we discussed meds pt became uncertain abt one of them – isn't sure if it's supposed to be taken once or twice daily, what time of day, or exact dose. Has the bottle but said label is worn off or hard to read. Pt denies having missed doses but clearly confused abt proper administration. Advised to contact pharmacy or MD office to clarify before continuing. Also mentioned knee pain has been bothersome but that's pre-existing, not related to recent hospitalization. Will VM pharmacy to follow up on our end and confirm correct dosing back to pt.

POV call w/ daughter, pt 5d s/p d/c. Pt c/o no acute issues, denies fever, denies nausea, wound clean and dry. Daughter reports home phone # on file is incorrect - stated correct # is 555-0847 and requested we update chart. Notified to contact admissions to correct contact info. Pt instructed to call if any new concerns arise.

Pt called in for 12d post-d/c f/u. Denies new sx or concerns. States has not received any info re specialist appt yet, was told it would be arranged b4 discharge. Pt c/o no call or paperwork. Instructed pt to call discharge planner in AM, advised may take 1-2 wks to process. Pt agreeable, will f/u if no contact w/in 5d.

Pt called today 13d post-d/c. C/o not having heard back from lab re results. States was told results would be communicated but has not received any contact. Denies further sx. RN instructed pt to contact ordering provider's office directly to obtain results & confirm whether testing complete. VM left for provider team to follow up re: status of pending results.
POD 11 f/u call placed, pt answered. Denies c/o. States has not received appointment info for follow-up visit yet, unclear on where to go or when.

pt called to follow up POD#1. c/o frustration w/ CPAP mask fit & unable to get seal to feel comfortable. denies ability to adjust straps properly, states equipment feels loose & keeps slipping during sleep. instructed on proper mask positioning & strap tension, provided contact # for DME supplier for hands-on fitting assistance. pt receptive to reaching out. will f/u in 2 days.

POD#2 follow-up call w/ daughter at bedside. Pt has rx in hand but hasn't started yet - says wants to wait a few days to see how he feels off meds first. Daughter c/o he's been more confused today than yesterday but denies falls or chest pain. Instructed both on importance of starting abx as ordered, will VM back tomorrow to check in.

Pt called 2d post op s/p hernia repair. C/o redness and warmth at incision site. Denies fever. Pt reports area is weeping, notes some yellow drainage. Instructed pt to contact surgeon today, VM left w/ on-call.

Pt called c/o redness and warmth at lumbar surgical site s/p laminectomy 12d ago. Reports weeping drainage, describes as yellowish and foul-smelling. Denies fever but states pain at incision has worsened. Advised pt to contact surgeon today and VM left for same. Instructed to monitor closely and call back if drainage increases or spreads.
Pt VM left, callback requested.
Pt reached. Wheelchair DME ordered pre-D/C has not arrived. Pt states tried one call to vendor, wants RN to follow up on status and replacement options.
Pt called, states unable to pay for PT sessions dc'd set up for next week - asked about cost of copay and frequency, denies able to cover expense at this time.

Called pt at home to f/u post-op d77 s/p appendectomy. Pt doing well, no fevers, incision healing fine per report. Some lingering abd tenderness but improving, taking Tylenol PRN. Chatted about the grandkids visiting from out of state, sounds like nice weather where they are. Mentioned our weather has been unusually hot this year. Pt then brought up that he's taking something for pain but can't quite remember if he's supposed to take it with food or on empty stomach, and not sure if it's one pill twice a day or what exactly. Didn't have bottle in front of him during call. Educated on checking label or calling pharmacy but also will need to verify med list at office - sounds like possible confusion re: dosing and timing of current analgesic. Advised pt to call pharmacy or reach out if any new concerns. VM left for primary care to reconcile med list given 77 days out and pt unable to confirm current regimen details.

Phone f/u from caregiver of 85yo pt s/p CABG POD 65. Caregiver states pt doing well overall, no acute c/o. During call noted chart flagged - appears pt has 2 records in system from recent hospitalization, same admission dates. Caregiver not aware of issue. Instructed caregiver to contact scheduling to verify which record is primary. Advised will reach out to medical records to clarify before next scheduled visit.

Pt called in for post-d/c f/u. Initially reached at home, pt c/o abdominal pain x 3 days, denies nausea or vomiting. Pain intermittent, describes as crampy, no relation to recent surgery. Denies fever, changes in appetite, or recent dietary changes. Taking OTC antacid PRN w/ minimal relief. Pt instructed to contact PCP if pain worsens or if fever develops. Advised to follow up with PCP within 1 week. No acute findings noted during call. Plan: patient education provided, will f/u again in 2 days per protocol.
Post-d/c call attempt 5 days s/p discharge. VM left requesting pt callback at convenience.

POC w/ caregiver for 85yo pt 13d s/p appendectomy. Caregiver reports pt c/o incision "not staying closed" - states sutures/staples appear to be coming apart and edges of wound separating. Caregiver notes increased drainage and some opening visible at site. Advised caregiver to contact surgeon today, instructed to keep area clean and dry. Will follow up tomorrow AM.

Called pt's daughter to follow up on post-op status s/p cholecystectomy 18 days ago. Daughter reports pt having a real rough time getting around the house, can't seem to get up from chair without a lot of pain and struggling. When trying to walk to the kitchen daughter says pt is very slow and unsteady, holding onto walls. Daughter mentioned weather's been nice which is good bc pt's been stuck inside mostly. When asked about specific pain c/o generalized soreness around the incision site but says the pain meds help some. Also going on about how her other daughter is coming to visit next week and maybe they can finally get mom outside for a bit. We talked through some of the mobility issues and I encouraged daughter to make sure pt is doing the gentle movements we discussed at discharge, taking it slow. Pt denies fever, denies increased redness or drainage at incision. Daughter worried pt not progressing fast enough compared to what we told them to expect, thought by day 18 pt would be moving better. VM left for pt's primary care to check in.

Pt called today POD 19 s/p CABG. Reports having difficulty w/ soft diet, states foods feel difficult to swallow and causing mild discomfort in chest area. Denies N/V or choking. Currently tolerating liquids and ice chips without issue. Instructed pt to continue current intake, RTC with surgeon if symptoms worsen or persist beyond next few days. Will call back in 3 days to reassess.

Pt called by family member to follow up s/p discharge. Reports meds arrived at pharmacy & she picked them up, but hasn't started taking them yet per instructions. Discussed importance of starting regimen. Pt willing to begin tonight. VM left with daughter for reinforcement.

Pt's caregiver called for f/u, pt is 78 days s/p hernia repair and doing well overall, incision healing fine no concerns there. Caregiver mentioned pt has been feeling nauseous on and off for about 3 weeks now, not related to the surgery site or anything acute. Pt denies any n/v immediately after discharge or in the first couple months which is good. Says the nausea comes and goes, worse in afternoons, pt tried some ginger tea and that helps a bit. Has been taking his usual meds no changes there. Caregiver also mentioned it's been raining all week where they are, roads have been terrible. Pt denies fever, denies diarrhea, appetite is down a little but pt is eating. Mentioned his daughter is visiting next month which is nice. No abd pain, no changes in bowel habits otherwise. Caregiver to monitor and call back if worsens or if pt develops any other symptoms, advised to reach out sooner if needed.
41d s/p cholecystectomy, caregiver reports pt c/o RLQ pain x 2 wks, describes as crampy, intermittent, denies relationship to surgical site, no fever, VM left re: onset timing and radiation.

Pt's daughter called on 1D post-dc, pt doing okay overall but daughter reports concern abt pt attending follow-up with ortho. Daughter mentioned pt's meds refill is being covered by insurance no problem, but she's worried abt the actual appointment visit itself—said copay is $50 which pt just can't swing right now. Pt on fixed income, daughter explained, and w the holiday expenses and PT starting she doesn't have the flexibility. She asked if there's any way to delay the visit or find a sliding scale clinic. Also mentioned her own car needs work, weather's been awful here, nephew had the flu. Reiterated that meds themselves r fine just the copay for the ortho follow-up visit itself. Discussed that early intervention would be better, encouraged daughter to contact ortho office directly abt financial assistance programs before pt misses the appointment.

Called pt this evening, she was doing laundry when phone rang, says she's been feeling pretty good overall since d/c 53 days ago, hysterectomy site healed up nicely no drainage or anything. Weather's been nice where she is, we talked about her daughter's new job for a bit. Then mentioned she's been having some crampy pain in her belly, mostly lower abdomen, started about a week ago and comes and goes. I asked where exactly and she pointed to more the lower left side away from where they did the surgery, not at the incision site itself. She denies fever, denies nausea or vomiting, able to eat regular diet, BMs normal. Pain is maybe 4/10, not using the leftover pain meds from the procedure, just taking Tylenol PRN when it's bothersome. Tried to reach PCP today she said but they're booked, wanted advice before calling back. Pain doesn't seem related to the hysterectomy recovery from what she describes, sounds more localized to different area. Advised to follow up with PCP given ongoing discomfort and to call 911 if worsens or fever develops.

Pt called to check in s/p discharge 5d ago. States wound care nurse was supposed to come today but denies anyone has come; no dressing supplies delivered either. Pt knows how to do dressing changes from hosp but waiting for scheduled visits.

Pt called with c/o nausea x 3 weeks, denies relation to surgery. States started ~2 wks after d/c, not associated w/ meals or activity. Denies vomiting. Appetite decreased but tolerating POs. RTC to see PCP given timing remote from lami s/p 58d ago. VM left for MD regarding sx onset and labs prn.

Pt called from home, 8d s/p discharge, doing reasonably well overall. Weather been nice here, pt says warm for this time of year. Son visited yesterday. Pt c/o persistent abdominal discomfort since yesterday morning, described as dull ache in lower abd, rates 5-6/10. Denies N/V, denies constipation or diarrhea, bowels moving normally. Denies fever, wound healing well from prior surgery months ago so this is unrelated to that. Pain not relieved by PRN meds, tried heating pad VM. Abd soft per pt, no trauma. Encouraged fluids, advised to call MD if worsens or fever develops, pt agreeable. Will follow up ROV in 2-3 days. Also mentioned her arthritis flaring with the humidity, unrelated but wanted to mention.

Pt called re: pain mgmt post-op. Denies specific pain at incision site which is healing well per pt. C/o diffuse abdominal discomfort & generalized achiness that is persisting despite adhering to prescribed analgesic regimen q4-6h. States not localized to surgical area. Taking meds as directed, pain not resolving. VM left w/ pt to call back if worsens or new sx develop. ROV to reassess in 1 wk.

Pt c/o persistent pain in operative knee despite strict adherence to prescribed analgesia regimen. 47 days s/p total knee arthroplasty. Pain diffuse throughout joint, not localized to incision line; incision well-healed per pt. Tried OTC NSAIDs PRN in addition to current meds without relief. Advised to contact orthopedic surgeon given pain unresponsive to current management plan.

POD#4 call to daughter. Pt has card appt scheduled for 10/18 at 2pm but states cannot make that day - daughter will be at work and no one else available to drive. Daughter asked about rescheduling. VM to cardiology scheduled - advised will need to call back to set new date.

Pt called c/o ongoing knee pain s/p discharge. Denies med issues. When discussed PT referral, pt stated unable to attend bc cannot afford copay for visit. Reviewed options but pt adamant - financial situation tight right now, stated even one visit copay would strain budget. Encouraged pt to call back if status changes. VM sent to case manager re: community resources.

Pt called reporting doing well overall s/p hernia repair 56d ago, incision healing fine per pt, denies drainage or increasing pain. Mentioned weather has been nice, family visiting next month. When asked about wound care pt stated "I thought someone was supposed to call me about that" - denies ever receiving a call or info about any wound care visits or supplies needed. Advised getting clear on what was ordered, pt to contact surgeon's office to confirm what was supposed to be set up and why he hasn't heard from anyone. Will attempt to reach surgery clinic to verify orders and coordinate.

Caregiver called pt day 14 post DC. Pt has cardiology f/u appt scheduled for next wk but reports too fatigued to leave home that day - having increased SOB w/ minimal exertion past 3-4 days. Caregiver able to drive but pt c/o doesn't feel safe traveling in car given breathing difficulties. Discussed w/ caregiver - may need earlier eval vs appt reschedule pending symptom trend. Will f/u VM to pt tomorrow re: status.
VM left 10/15 at 1430, asked pt to call back today regarding post-op follow-up. ROV.

Pt reached on callback. States received rx from pharmacy 3 wks ago, got it filled without issue. However, has not started the medication yet b/c pt reports wants to see how knee continues to do without it first. Discussed importance of taking as prescribed post-op. Pt states will reconsider and call back if has questions.

Pt's caregiver called during post-op check at 35d s/p cholecystectomy. Pt doing well, denies fever, nausea, or wound concerns. Caregiver reports pt unable to attend f/u appointment due to cost of copay and time off work - not financial issue w/ medications. Instructed on VM for surgical team if acute concern develops. ROV advised.
VM left 2/13 @ 1430 requesting pt call back re f/u appt. No response.

Pt called back. States doing well, no c/o re abdominal pain or wound issues s/p colectomy 62d ago. Has had good appetite, bowel fxn normal per pt report. Mentioned been rainy and gloomy lately, mentioned daughter visiting from out of state next month which is nice. Pt has scheduled follow-up appt w/ surgeon 3/4 at 230p but says cannot attend that day due to having committed to drive grandchildren to school event all day, recurring appointment that pt takes very seriously. Pt able to do phone follow-up or reschedule for different day. Denies other barriers to appt. No new meds or complications. Offered to check w/ surgeon's office re alternate dates or remote visit option. Pt agrees will wait for call back from office. Lives w/ daughter currently, no transportation issues noted.

POD 10 s/p appendectomy. Pt c/o intermittent nausea this past week, worse in evenings, denies n/v since discharge but reports feeling queasy when eating solid foods. No fever, no abdominal pain. Attributes to lingering effects from surgery.

Pt called reporting persistent generalized pain despite compliance w/ prescribed regimen. Denies localized incision tenderness or drainage. Pain distributed throughout body, not limited to surgical site. Taking all meds as directed including PRN analgesics. Advised to contact surgeon if pain worsens or focal symptoms develop.

VM'd caregiver 1630h, returned call 1645h. Caregiver reports pt doing okay overall, wound looks clean & dry, some mild ecchymosis around incision but staples intact & no erythema. Talked about the weather here being unusually warm. Caregiver mentioned she herself has been dealing w/ lower back issues, been a rough week taking care of pt and managing the house. When asked about pain pt taking meds on schedule as prescribed q6h but caregiver says pain is not really improving much, says it's been constant throughout the day even when pt takes the regimen regularly, not just at the incision area but more generalized type of achiness & soreness. Pt denies any nausea or new swelling. Caregiver will monitor closely & call back if any concerns arise.

Pt called back to check in post-discharge, 64 days s/p appendectomy. Was having decent weather where he is, asked about my drive. Went through med list - flagged the antibiotic that was sent to pharmacy after discharge. Pt confirms he has the bottle at home, got it filled right away. I asked when he started it and he said he hasn't actually taken any yet, just been holding onto it. Said he was feeling better pretty quick after surgery so figured he didn't really need it. Denies any c/o of fever, chills, or wound issues. Reminded him of importance of finishing the full course as prescribed despite feeling well. Pt acknowledged and said he'll start taking it today. Also mentioned his arthritis acting up from the cold snap but otherwise doing okay, grandkids visiting next week.
VM left 10/15 1430, pt called back ROV same day 1645

Pt c/o picked up Rx from pharmacy 10/8 POD 7, has bottle at home but states hasn't started yet - concerned about side effects after reading online, wants to discuss w/ MD before beginning. Encouraged pt to contact surgeon's office to review risks/benefits. Pt denies barriers to getting to pharmacy, denies cost issues. Will follow up post-conversation w/ provider.

Called pt's daughter who reports pt doing well overall s/p TKA 76d ago. Pt ambulating, pain controlled on current regimen. Daughter states wound looks clean and dry but mentions no one from VNA has been to house and she's unsure when dressing changes are supposed to happen. Reviewed d/c paperwork and no orders for home wound care are present in chart. Contacted orthopedic clinic to issue stat referral for wound assessment and supply delivery. Pt daughter instructed to call if any redness, warmth, drainage, or fever develops prior to visit. Will follow up in 48hrs to confirm services initiated.

Pt called by VM ROV. 87yo denies c/o but states unable to afford PT scheduled for mobility assessment s/p discharge - "can't manage the copay right now" and reports daughter concerned about transportation costs. Pt ambulating at home, appears stable. Advised to call MD office re: rescheduling options and community resources. Will attempt contact in 1 week.

Caregiver c/o pt has post-op hernia repair F/U appt scheduled but cannot make time due to conflicts w/ caregiver availability that day; explored rescheduling options, pt willing to coordinate alternate date.

Pt called. 55d s/p TKA, doing well w/ ROM and ambulation. Reports been having intermittent nausea past 2 wks, denies vomiting. States unrelated to surgery, happening mostly in AM and evening. Denies new meds, diet change, or abdominal pain. Last ate solid food this AM w/o issue. Encouraged to f/u w/ PCP for workup given timing remote from procedure. Pt called d/c POD 11 c/o feeling dizzy and lightheaded, especially when standing up from chair. Denies loss of consciousness but reports feeling like he might pass out yesterday morning. Called pt's daughter this AM re f/u post hysterectomy, pt doing OK overall but reports she's been feeling pretty queasy since getting home 15 days ago, not really improving much. She's keeping food down most of the time when she does eat but says even the smell of chicken makes her turn green which is weird because that's normally her favorite. Daughter thinks maybe it's lingering from the anesthesia since she had such a rough recovery room experience and was groggy for hours after waking up. I told her to keep monitoring and that some folks do have delayed nausea from surgery meds, and to call back if it gets worse or if she develops fever or abd distention.

Pt called reporting doing well post-op s/p cholecystectomy 54d ago, denies pain or complications. States unable to schedule f/u appointment at this time due to cost of copay. POV c/o redness and warmth at sternotomy incision site, pt's daughter reports weeping and what appears to be pus drainage x since dc 3d ago s/p CABG. Denies fever, pt states area is tender. Pt called in re post-op f/u s/p TKA. States doing okay overall but having harder time than she thought getting around the house. Pt called today 55d s/p hysterectomy. Reports doing well overall, c/o mild residual achiness but manageable. When asked about monitoring, pt states not doing daily weights or BP checks as instructed. pt called today s/p d/c 10d. states unable to afford f/u apt given copay, asking if care can proceed w/o it. also reports confusion re: wound care - DC summary says dry dressing changes daily but cardiology called yesterday w/ different instructions for moisture barrier. pt unsure which to follow, concerned about wound healing. instructed pt to contact PCP office for clarification, emphasized importance of consistent technique. discussed financial counseling resources, offered VM referral.

Pt called to report redness, warmth and purulent drainage from appendectomy incision site x 3 days. Denies fever, abd pain, or other s/s. Called pt this AM, had just gotten in from running errands. Doing well overall s/p laminectomy, back pain much improved, no radiation down leg anymore which is great. Will ROV in 2 wks.

Called pt today 42d s/p hernia repair. Doing ok overall, says weather's been nice where he is. Mentioned his daughter just started college which is exciting. Daughter called to follow up s/p d/c 8 days ago. Pt c/o persistent abd pain diffuse across lower abdomen, denies fever or recent trauma. Pt called x15d s/p cholecystectomy reporting ongoing nausea, worse in AM, denies vomiting. States eating small frequent meals helps. No fever, denies abd distension or severe pain. Pt c/o difficulty arranging transportation to scheduled f/u appt. Denies financial barriers & states not insurance/coverage issue. Pt has no personal vehicle & no one available to provide ride. Pt called today, 6d s/p d/c. Reports feeling "fuzzy" and confused about what day it is, having trouble remembering when he ate breakfast. Wife concerned he's "not himself." Denies fever, headache, other new symptoms.

Caregiver called re: post-op TKA f/u. Called pt at home POD 9 s/p discharge. Caregiver answered, stated pt does not wish to participate in follow-up calls and asked to be removed from call list. Caregiver declined to provide clinical update. VM left requesting contact if concerns arise.

Pt called reporting doing okay overall s/p discharge but having difficulty w/ new statin script. States insurance approved it but copay is $60/mo and having trouble making that work on fixed income. Pt c/o walker not received yet s/p d/c 5d ago, states equipment company said it would arrive but has not. Instructed pt to call DME vendor directly to track shipment, will ROV.

pt called requesting assistance w/ transport to future appointments. states unable to sit upright s/p appendectomy, remains bed-bound and requires stretcher or wheelchair van. denies this is coverage issue - explicitly states needs actual transport arranged as cannot transfer independently into regular vehicle. no medical transport currently in place. advised pt of need to contact scheduling and case mgmt today to arrange prior to next appt.

Reached pt at home today, doing fairly well post-op s/p CABG 66 days ago. Denies chest pain or SOB at rest, ambulating around house without issue though gets winded going up stairs which pt says is improving. Mentioned the weather has been nice which helped him get outside a bit. Wife doing well also. Wife mentioned they may need to look at other living arrangements but housing market is tight and finances are strained post-surgery. Pt also complaining of occasional indigestion which we discussed is likely dietary, taking Tums PRN. No fever, no wound issues, dressing came off without problem. Advised pt to document mold issue with landlord in writing and escalate if needed, also discussed importance of dry clean environment during cardiac recovery. Pt agreeable to call back if housing situation worsens or if develops any cardiac symptoms. Will follow up in one week.
Pt c/o ongoing abd pain x several wks, denies relation to choleystectomy site, location vague. States pain present at rest, denies fever/drainage/N/V, currently managing w/ OTC analgesics PRN.
Called pt residence 2:15pm, no answer. VM left requesting return call to clinic. Caregiver to follow up.

Reached caregiver at home, pt in background. Caregiver states weather has been beautiful finally after all that rain last week, mentioned grandson visiting next month from up north. Pt c/o still waiting to hear back about the tests they did before coming home, daughter says they never got a call from anyone with results. Caregiver unclear which tests exactly but knows dr ordered something during hospital stay. Pt denies any new symptoms, eating ok, temp normal this AM. Reminded caregiver that results may take several days s/p discharge but husband sounded concerned so I offered to check with records. Will attempt to locate any pending results from last admission and call back pt within 24hrs. Caregiver asked about pain meds too, pt taking them as prescribed, no issues there. ROV high priority to track down what labs or imaging were ordered and communicate status back to family.

pt called today, 2 days post cholecystectomy. doing ok overall, wound looks good she says but having a lot of trouble with the pain at the incision site. states it's not getting better w/ the percocet she was sent home on, taking it every 4-6 hrs as prescribed but says the pain just stays there. asked if she's been icing it and keeping activity minimal, she said yea but it's still pretty sore. also mentioned her teenager just got a new job which is great, been dealing w/ some weather out there too has been hot. denies fever, denies increased redness or drainage from the site, denies n/v. pain is sharp when she moves around too much but even at rest it's nagging. reviewed taking the med w/ food, offered suggestion to try ice packs more frequently, encouraged her to call back or go to ED if develops signs of infection. will VM surgeon's office to report inadequate pain control and see if need to adjust regimen or schedule earlier follow-up visit. pt said she understood and will touch base after speaks w/ surgeon.

Pt called 67d s/p colectomy. Denies acute issues, pain well controlled. Reports having rx list but pharmacy says insurer won't process meds pending prior auth from dr office. Pt contacted dr office yesterday, told them to follow up w/ insurance company. Currently unable to fill scripts, awaiting resolution. Advised pt to call dr office again if not resolved by EOW.

POD 78 s/p lumbar laminectomy. Pt c/o pain but denies taking prescribed pain med, states has script filled but concerned about taking it "too much" and worried about dependency. Also reports living situation unstable - staying with daughter currently but daughter says house only temporary, may need to move again in few weeks. Pt lives alone usually, concerned about managing stairs and daily activities at home alone once discharged from daughter's place. ROV medication compliance and social situation. VM to case mgmt re housing options and follow up pain control plan next week.

Pt called reporting ongoing nausea since d/c 6 days s/p hysterectomy, worse in AM. Denies fever, abd pain, or food intolerance. Tried ginger tea and small frequent meals yesterday with minimal relief. Started taking the ondansetron PRN which helped briefly. No episodes of actual vomiting but feels queasy most of day. Advised re: anesthesia effects lingering, encouraged increased fluids, discussed VM if worsens.

Called pt at home, 55 days s/p appendectomy, pt states doing okay overall but having trouble with the walker at home, says he can't quite figure out how to adjust the height properly and feels unsteady when he uses it so has been avoiding it mostly. Mentioned the weather's been nice which is good. Also mentioned his daughter visited last week which was lovely. Talked about TV shows for a bit. Then pt brought up that he also has a nebulizer that the respiratory therapist left and he's not really clear on how to use it, hasn't been using it much bc he's confused about the mask part and where the medicine goes. Denies falling, denies c/o new pain, states incision healing well. Pt mentioned his neighbor had some trouble too, kind of went off on tangent about their knee surgery. VM left with pt re: walker adjustment, discussed calling OT for in-home eval and also suggested he call respiratory to get someone to show him the nebulizer setup, pt receptive to plan. To follow up in 1 week.

Called by daughter this AM. Pt 73d s/p appendectomy doing well overall, no fever or drainage. Daughter reports pt having difficulty w/ new abx script—insurance approved but copay $285/mo, pt on fixed income. Pt currently taking every other day to make it last, skipping doses on wkends. Counseled re: infection risk, offered pharmacy benefit check & PAP resources. VM left for MD re: alternative abx options or samples.

Pt called today 2 days post-op CABG. Was doing OK initially but having real trouble getting around the house, says legs feel weak when she tries to stand up from the chair and nearly fell yesterday when transferring to the bathroom. Mentioned it's been cold and rainy out so hasn't gotten outside yet but worried she's not progressing like she expected. Also c/o general fatigue and some confusion about her post-op meds which we reviewed. During conversation she mentioned her daughter is visiting next week which is good support. Towards end of call she stated she has cardiology follow-up appt scheduled for next Tues at 10am but can't make it that day because her daughter's flight gets in late Monday and won't be available to drive her. Pt denies chest pain, SOB at rest, or wound issues. Instructed her on activity progression, safety with transfers, and to call if any red flags develop. Needs to contact cardiology office ASAP regarding appt reschedule - will try VM for them if pt doesn't connect.
VM left. Pt to call back when available. Contact made on 2nd attempt.

Pt c/o incision site s/p TKA opening up, sutures coming apart. States area around knee not holding together. Advised pt to contact surgeon today, ROV to ortho office or ED if unable to reach. Pt agrees.

Called pt's caregiver today per protocol, 4 days s/p discharge. Caregiver reports pt doing okay overall, wound healing well, no c/o pain but mentioned it's been chilly out here lately, asked about our office parking situation which was random. Main issue when we got down to it is pt is confused about what he can eat and drink at this point—caregiver states pt keeps asking her what's allowed, especially about coffee and soft foods, wasn't totally clear on the discharge instructions. Caregiver also mentioned her own knee has been acting up, unrelated but she brought it up, anyway we went back over the dietary restrictions that should've been covered in the hospital discharge packet. Pt denies N/V, denies fever, tolerating POs okay when given specific guidance. Reviewed what foods/fluids are appropriate at this stage and caregiver verbalized understanding, will reinforce w/ pt. VM attempted to clarify the discharge diet sheet but will also send written summary via mail to ensure no further confusion. Pt ambulatory, vitals stable per caregiver, no acute concerns identified otherwise.
Pt called back to voicemail left yesterday. ROV answering now.

Pt doing well post-d/c but states major problem is getting to tx appts multiple times per week. Receives infusion tx 3x/wk, has reliable insurance coverage and says cost is not issue. Main barrier is arranging reliable transport that often - cannot depend on family for repeated pickups and Uber/taxi cost adds up fast. Pt frustrated because wants to comply with tx plan but says "can't figure out logistics of getting there that many times." Discussed resources w/ pt, will provide SW consult for transportation assistance at f/u visit.
87d s/p lumbar laminectomy. Caregiver c/o pt unsure of dose, frequency, and timing of current medication holding. Instructed to contact PCP office for clarification prior to next fill.

Pt called for post-d/c f/u 38d s/p appendectomy. Doing well overall, denies complications. Reports difficulty obtaining foods that meet the prescribed diet - states grocery store limited in options & transportation to specialty market problematic. Lives alone, family unable to assist w/ shopping. Rec'd list of mail order services & local delivery programs, pt to try & call back w/ questions.
VM left 11/15 requesting pt to call back regarding post-op follow-up. Pt reached today 11/16 @ 1430.

Pt c/o some drainage from surgical site, states she has been changing gauze daily per discharge instructions but denies pain or fever. When asked about wound care visits, pt reports she never received a call to schedule and said no supplies have been delivered to home. Instructed pt on next steps to arrange nursing visits and dressing supplies. Will follow up.

Pt called w/ c/o of swelling in legs x 1 wk, notes shoes feeling tighter & ankles puffy bilat. Denies pain or redness. Weight up 7 lbs since DC 52 days ago s/p colectomy. Pt ambulating ok, denies SOB or chest pain. RN advised pt to contact PCP for eval, discussed leg elevation & encouraged fluid intake, will follow up VM in 3 days.

Pt called, s/p d/c 5d. Has ortho f/u appt scheduled for next week but states car in shop - will have access to vehicle by then but prior obligations may conflict. Reevaluated timeline w/ pt, she able to reschedule. Will contact ortho office to move appt, pt to confirm new date VM or call back.

Pt called 7d post-dc, reports unable to fill new med due to cost. Discussed w/ pt that copay too high, stated cannot budget for it right now. Encouraged pt to contact PCP re: formulary alternatives or assistance programs. Pt agreed to call office tomorrow. No acute c/o at this time, tolerating current meds at home.
VM left 11/15 PM, pt's daughter called back this AM
Caregiver reports pt started having dizzy spells yesterday, denies falls, states began after started new beta blocker 5 days ago s/p discharge, holding med pending provider callback

Pt called today, 13d s/p colectomy. Reports continued upset stomach & feeling like she might throw up, especially in the mornings. Denies fever, abd pain, or diarrhea. Tolerating soft diet OK otherwise. Advised to continue small frequent meals, ginger ale PRN, and monitor symptoms. Will contact surgeon's office if worsens or if unable to keep fluids down.
VM left 1430 pt's daughter called back at 1515 requesting to reschedule earlier callback as pt having trouble overnight

Spoke w/ daughter who is primary caregiver at home. Pt doing generally well since d/c 58 days ago from lumbar laminectomy, walking more, back pain much improved. Daughter mentioned weather has been really nice finally, they took pt out to yard yesterday. Then asked about pt c/o chest feeling tight like pressure especially when pt gets up too fast or bends forward. Started noticing it maybe 3-4 days ago, worse in evening hrs. Pt takes ASA daily per prior d/c paperwork. No fever. Pt also mentioned some weird knee pain unrelated but daughter says that's been there forever not new. Tried to clarify onset of chest pressure - daughter thinks maybe related to pt overdoing it w/ activity or sleeping weird but honestly not sure. Advised daughter to have pt call PCP today and given 911 precautions for any acute SOB or crushing sensation. Will attempt ROV call in 2 days.
VM left, pt to call back when available
Pt states received different instructions from surgeon vs. case mgmt re: activity restrictions post-op. Clarified restrictions w/ case mgmt, will send written summary. Pt verbalized understanding.

Called to do post-op check in on pt 36d s/p colectomy. Pt answered but said we had wrong number on file - she said this isn't the number she gave them at discharge and when we called back later vm said line was disconnected. Asked her to verify current contact and she gave different number, said she'd been trying to figure out why we never called her earlier, was getting worried. Went ahead and did assessment over phone anyway since we had her, pt c/o minimal pain at incision site, denies fever or drainage, eating regular diet. She was actually pretty chatty, went off on tangent about how this heat wave is killing her garden and her sister's been having car trouble, complained her back's been sore but thinks it's from sleeping wrong not surgery related. Got vitals as best we could on phone, VSS, pt ambulating around house fine. Will need to follow up with correct contact info in system before next scheduled call.
Called pt residence at 2pm, no answer. VM left requesting callback today.

Spoke w/ daughter (caregiver) at 4:15pm. Pt 87yo s/p colectomy 72d ago. Daughter reports meds pt was d/c on have not arrived - pharmacy says waiting on insurance prior auth. Daughter unsure how long delay will be. Instructed caregiver to contact pharmacy and insurance directly for status, provided pharmacy#. Will ROV tomorrow AM to check on med delivery status.
Initial attempt 1400 VM left, pt to call back

Pt called back at 1445. States incision area on chest "doesn't look right" and that the edges are pulling apart where the stitches are. Denies fever but says there's some drainage, clear to slightly yellow colored. Pt concerned and asking when he should come in. Lives with wife who's been helping with wound care, she agrees it looks different than it did few days ago. Pt doing okay otherwise, back to sitting in recliner more now which is good, says weather's been nice so he sat out on porch yesterday afternoon even though he's not supposed to do stairs yet. Denies chest pain, no SOB at rest. Denies any recent cough or sick contacts though mentions daughter visited from out of state this past weekend. Wife gave him Tylenol this AM for some shoulder aching he's been having, unrelated to surgery. Pt asking about the incision urgently, wants to know if this is normal or if he needs to be seen sooner than the scheduled follow-up appt next week. Advised pt to keep area clean and dry, not to pull at it, and call surgeon's office first thing AM or go to ED if worsening/fever/increased drainage develops overnight. Pt understood. Wife will monitor and they have surgeon's number.

Pt called today 90d s/p R TKA. C/o increased shortness of breath x 2-3 wks, present at rest & worsens w/ activity. Denies chest pain, fever, or leg swelling. Ambulating indoors but limited by SOB. Encouraged to call PCP today given onset & duration. VM left for orthosurg clinic re post-op course. Advised ROV urgent care if dyspnea worsens or chest pain develops.

Pt c/o still having trouble getting around and transferring - slower than expected s/p surgery. Also flagged that taking metoprolol both from discharge papers and has been on it at home - unclear which dose pt currently on. Advised pt to contact PCP today to clarify med list prior to restarting any cardiac meds.
VM left, pt to call back, answered 1420.
POD#2 s/p chole, pt c/o redness and warmth around incision site, reports weeping/draining yellow stuff. Advised to f/u w/ surgeon today, call office now.

Pt called today 40d s/p colectomy. Reports doing well physically, denies pain, drains removed without issue. States needs colonoscopy f/u per GI but cannot afford the copay and deductible at this time - already met max out of pocket with recent hospitalization. Discussed options for sliding scale clinic and financial counselor referral, pt agreed. Will VM card with resources.
VM left on first attempt, pt's daughter called back approx 1.5 hrs later per ROV.

7d s/p discharge. Spoke w/ daughter who reports pt c/o severe muscle cramps in legs & feet starting 2 days ago, did not have prior to hosp admit. Daughter thinks may be related to new statin started at discharge. Pt denies falls or inability to ambulate but cramps waking him at night. Advised daughter to contact MD re: possible med adjustment, instructed to call back if worsens or develops weakness.

Caregiver called for post-dc f/u s/p hernia repair. Pt doing well overall, denies fever or increased pain. Caregiver reports no wound care nurse has visited and unsure if supplies were arranged - says pt expected someone to come check incision but no one has shown up. VM left for discharge coordinator to verify orders and expedite services.

Pt called today, POD#3 s/p hernia repair. C/o persistent pain at incision site, rates 6/10 at rest, worse with activity. States taking oxycodone q4h and ibuprofen PRN but pain not improving. Denies fever, drainage, or spreading redness. Discussed that some post-op discomfort expected but will notify surgeon tomorrow given inadequate control on current regimen and early timeline post-procedure. Advised ice, rest, contact VM if worsening.
Pt c/o no answer on first attempt, VM left asking pt to call back at convenience. ROV today.

Pt called back per VM. S/P cholecystectomy 63d ago, healing well overall. Denies fever, infection c/o, or abd pain. Endorses pressure/tightness in chest x several days, worse with activity, better with rest. Denies SOB, nausea, diaphoresis. Pt on ASA PRN, denies taking it for this episode. Advised urgent eval given age and sx pattern, pt agreeable to call PCP today or go to ED if worsens. Will follow up post-eval.

Spoke w/ caregiver, pt 8d s/p DC. Caregiver reports pt is not tracking well, seems confused about what day it is and getting lost in own home which is new. Also called back asking if ok to have soup and water, unsure what safe to take in now. Denies fever, pain, N/V. Advised caregiver to contact MD re mental status change and gave brief summary of discharge diet. Caregiver will monitor and call back if worsening.

pt called today, 5d s/p disch. reports confusion re: BP meds - cardiology told him to continue lisinopril but discharge paperwork says d/c it. denies chest pain, SOB. also noted taking amlodipine at home from prior, still taking discharge amlodipine - asked which one to take. instructed pt to hold discharge amlodipine, verify lisinopril restart w/ cardiology before friday, msg left w/ PCP to clarify. pt tolerate ok otherwise.

Called pt's caregiver for post-discharge f/u 5d s/p discharge. Caregiver reports pt has filled meds but states not started yet due to wanting to "see how I feel first" before adding more pills to routine. Advised on importance of starting as prescribed and timing per DC instructions. Caregiver verbalized understanding and agreed to encourage pt to initiate today. VM left if further q's or concerns.
VM left 10/22 at 1430, no answer on line. Pt requested call back end of day.

Pt c/o right knee incision starting to open at lateral edge, edges coming apart. Denies fever, drainage, or increased pain. Advised pt to contact ortho office today, VM left for on-call if unable to reach clinic. S/p TKA 11d ago. ROV per RN protocol.

Pt called reporting fever and chills x 3 days, temp 101.2 yesterday. c/o intermittent night sweats, denies other sx. S/p hysterectomy 57 days ago. Pt unclear on what warrants ED visit vs when to call office, stated "not sure if fever is normal or what I should do." Instructed on fever precautions, advised to call office tomorrow, provided ED precautions.

Pt called today. Has appt scheduled w/ cardio on 3/22 but states unable to make that day - mentioned transportation is difficult this time of yr. Denies other barriers to attending. VM to be left w/ surgery scheduler to discuss options. RTC when changes confirmed.

Pt called in for 53d post-op f/u s/p hysterectomy. 85 yo states started having pressure in center of chest x 2 days, worse w/ movement, denies radiation or SOB. denies associated nausea, sweating, or palpitations. on home meds including ASA. VM left for MD call back re: eval, advised pt to seek emergent care if worsens or any dyspnea develops.

Pt called in, doing well post op from knee replacement 51 days ago, ambulating independently per pt report, minimal pain managed with tylenol PRN, denies swelling or redness. VM left for medical records to verify no duplicate charts in system, will ROV pt after clarification.
VM left 1/15 at 2:45pm requesting pt contact office regarding post-d/c check-in. Pt to call back at convenience.

Pt called back this AM. States doing well since d/c 12d ago, wound healing appropriately, denies fever or unusual drainage. During review of recent labs and encounter dates pt and RN identified that pt appears to have duplicate records in system - pt reports seeing documentation from same hospital visit filed under two different encounter numbers. Flagged for medical records review and consolidation. Advised pt no action needed on their end.
Pt called post s/p hernia repair, 62d post-d/c. C/o feeling very tired and weak, reports not able to do much at home, denies other concerns.

VM to caregiver 8d s/p DC. Pt has not recd RX for pain mgmt, contacted pharmacy twice, no record of script sent. Caregiver reports pt c/o increased pain, running out of current supply. Advised caregiver to contact prescriber's office directly to verify RX status and resend to pharmacy. Caregiver verbalized understanding, stated will call provider today.

Pt called to f/u s/p lumbar laminectomy 42d ago. Reports filled Rx for gabapentin at pharmacy 3w post-d/c but states "hasn't gotten around to starting it yet" - denies any barriers, says just hasn't opened bottle. Counseled on importance of pain management & encouraged to begin as prescribed. Pt verbalized understanding.

Pt called for routine f/u post-op day 42 s/p TKA. Says knee feeling better, pain controlled on current meds. Called by daughter at 1400. Pt reports new statin Rx filled 13d ago but only taking 1-2x/wk instead of daily - states copay manageable but overall med costs mounting w/ other refills, prioritizing which ones to take. Daughter reports they're stretching supply. Discussed pt's financial situation, insurance coverage options, need to contact PCP re: generic alternatives or assistance programs.

POD #12 pt called w/ c/o regarding his post-op status. States he has been unable to reach surgeon office, tried multiple times. Advised pt on proper follow-up contact procedures and VM left w/ surgeon's office.

Pt called requesting assistance s/p lumbar laminectomy 4d ago. Pt reports pain 7-8/10 at operative site, worsening with movement. Denies fever, drainage, or other concerning symptoms. Advised pt to contact surgeon if pain continues uncontrolled despite compliance w/ current meds. VM left for surgeon's office.

POD#8 s/p colectomy. Pt called with c/o difficulty tolerating advancement of diet. Reports nausea w/ attempts at soft foods, tried puree yesterday had to stop. Denies abd pain or distention. Tolerating sips of water and broth. Advised to hold advancement x24-48hrs, restart w/ clear liquids only, call back if worsening or unable to maintain fluids. VM left for surgeon.

POD#2 follow-up call, pt called in stating has not heard back from labs yet and unsure when results will be available. Pt called back today, 11d s/p DC. C/o doing okay overall but admits has not been checking BP or doing weights as instructed. States forgot about the routine & just hasn't gotten around to it. Reviewed importance of monitoring given recent hosp. Pt agreeable, will start weights daily in AM & BP checks BID. Will f/u in 1 wk to assess compliance.

Caregiver called for 65d post-op f/u s/p appendectomy. Pt reports ongoing nausea, denies vomiting but says feeling queasy off and on since discharge, worse w/ certain foods. Attempted VM ROV post-op f/u 70 days s/p hysterectomy. Caregiver reached, pt not available at time of call. Advised caregiver pt should expect follow-up contact within 24-48 hrs. No acute concerns reported by caregiver at this time. VM left on pt's line requesting return call to clinic.

Pt called today s/p CABG 79d. Reported taking metoprolol 25mg daily from prior refill plus metoprolol 25mg daily from discharge paperwork - pt says has two bottles. Pt called today 57d s/p colectomy. Reports generalized fatigue and weakness, says he's tired all the time and having trouble getting around the house. Pt called 72d s/p colectomy c/o new tremors in hands over past 2 days, suspects pain med refill causing it, denies other changes, instructed to hold next dose & contact PCP today.

Called residence 1430h, caregiver answered. Pt doing well generally, no acute c/o at this time. Discussed current meds and activity level, all appropriate per DC summary. Will call back in 2 weeks to check on wound healing.

Called back 1515h per caregiver request. Caregiver (daughter) reports pt eating ok overall, incision healing fine, denies fever or drainage. Pt called by caregiver, daughter, temp 98.6F. 20d s/p appendectomy doing okay overall but reports ongoing nausea, started immediately after surgery & anesthesia, waves come & go throughout day. Pt called back s/p VM left yesterday. ROV w/ pt re post-op status.

46d s/p appendectomy, incision healing well, denies fever/drainage/significant pain. VM left on 1st attempt, pt c/o no nurse or aide has shown up yet despite discharge orders placed.

ROV w/ pt today. States ordered home health still has not arrived, says he's been waiting 12 days since DC and hasn't heard from agency. Instructed pt to call agency directly w/ DC summary info and advised will escalate if services not initiated by EOW.
pt called back after VM left yesterday, reached today 2/15 at 1400.

POD 17 s/p hernia repair. Pt c/o ongoing nausea since discharge, denies vomiting but feeling queasy intermittently throughout day. Worse in AM, improving some w/ eating.
